Bicycle Twisting Crunch
The Bicycle Twisting Crunch is a core exercise that targets the abdominal muscles, particularly the obliques and rectus abdominis.
This exercise combines a cycling motion with a twisting crunch to engage the entire core area.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with hands behind your head and knees bent at 90 degrees
2. Alternate bringing opposite elbow to knee while extending the other leg
3. Maintain controlled movements and engage your core throughout
4. Continue alternating sides in a smooth pedaling motion
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your lower back pressed into the floor
2. Exhale as you twist and crunch
3. Avoid pulling on your neck with your hands
4. Focus on quality over quantity of repetitions
Fish Pose
Fish Pose is a yoga posture that stretches the chest, neck and abdominal muscles while opening the heart center.
This restorative backbend helps improve posture and relieve tension in the upper body.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with legs extended and arms alongside your body
2. Slide your hands under your hips, palms down
3. Press into your elbows to lift your chest and arch your upper back
4. Gently tilt your head backward to rest the crown on the floor
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your legs active and engaged
2. Breathe deeply into your chest
3. Don\'t force your head back if you feel neck strain
4. Hold for 15-30 seconds before releasing slowly
Hands In Air Dead Bug
The Hands In Air Dead Bug is a core stabilization exercise that improves coordination while strengthening the deep abdominal muscles.
This variation of the traditional Dead Bug challenges your core stability by removing the arm support.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with arms extended straight up toward ceiling
2. Lift knees to 90 degrees with shins parallel to floor
3. Slowly lower opposite arm and leg while maintaining core tension
4. Return to starting position and alternate sides
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your lower back pressed firmly into the mat
2. Move slowly with control
3. Exhale as you extend arm and leg
4. Stop if you feel your back arching off the floor
4 Point Tummy Vacuum Exercise
The 4 Point Tummy Vacuum is a deep core exercise that targets the transverse abdominis, the body\'s natural weightlifting belt.
This exercise improves core stability and can help flatten the abdominal appearance.
To perform the exercise:
1. Begin on all fours in tabletop position
2. Exhale completely and draw belly button toward spine
3. Hold this contraction while maintaining normal breathing
4. Maintain for 10-30 seconds before releasing
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your spine in neutral alignment
2. Don\'t hold your breath - breathe shallowly while holding
3. Focus on drawing in rather than sucking in
4. Progress by adding limb movements while maintaining contraction
Seated Flutter Kick
The Seated Flutter Kick is a core and hip flexor exercise performed in a seated position to target the lower abdominals.
This variation reduces neck strain compared to traditional lying flutter kicks.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the floor with hands slightly behind you for support
2. Lean back slightly and lift legs a few inches off the floor
3. Alternate small up-and-down kicks with each leg
4. Maintain controlled movements for desired duration
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged throughout
2. Avoid rounding your shoulders forward
3. Start with short durations (20-30 seconds)
4. For more challenge, lift hands off the floor
Seated Cable Twist
The Seated Cable Twist is an effective exercise that targets the obliques and improves rotational core strength.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on a bench or floor with your feet secured and hold a cable handle with both hands.
2. Keep your back straight and engage your core.
3. Twist your torso to one side while maintaining control.
4. Return to the center and twist to the opposite side.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid using momentum; focus on controlled movements.
2. Keep your abs engaged throughout the exercise.
3. Perform slow and steady reps for maximum effectiveness.
Bodyweight Kneeling Sissy Squat
The Bodyweight Kneeling Sissy Squat is an advanced quadriceps exercise that also engages the core.
To perform the exercise:
1. Kneel on the floor with your torso upright.
2. Lean back while keeping your body in a straight line.
3. Lower yourself until you feel a deep stretch in your quads.
4. Engage your thighs and core to return to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your hips extended throughout the movement.
2. Move slowly to maintain control and balance.
3. Avoid bending at the waist; maintain a straight posture.
Bow Pose
The Bow Pose is a yoga backbend that stretches the chest, shoulders, and abs while strengthening the back muscles.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your stomach and bend your knees, bringing your heels toward your glutes.
2. Reach back and grab your ankles with your hands.
3. Lift your chest and thighs off the ground, creating a bow shape.
4. Hold the position for a few breaths before releasing.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid straining your neck.
2. Engage your core and legs to maintain balance.
3. Breathe deeply to enhance the stretch.
Kneeling T-Spine Rotation
The Kneeling T-Spine Rotation improves thoracic spine mobility and enhances rotational movement.
To perform the exercise:
1. Get into an all-fours position with your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
2. Place one hand behind your head while keeping the other hand on the floor.
3. Rotate your torso, bringing your elbow toward the ceiling.
4. Return to the starting position and repeat on the other side.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your hips stable to isolate thoracic rotation.
2. Move in a controlled manner to prevent excessive lower back movement.
3. Perform slow, deliberate reps for optimal mobility benefits.
Standing Barbell Rollout
The Standing Barbell Rollout is an advanced core exercise that strengthens the abdominals, shoulders, and stability muscles.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand upright with a barbell placed on the floor in front of you.
2. Bend at the hips and grab the barbell with both hands, keeping your arms extended.
3. Slowly roll the barbell forward while maintaining core engagement.
4. Extend as far as you can while keeping control, then roll back to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core tight to prevent excessive lower back strain.
2. Move slowly and avoid jerking motions.
3. If needed, start with kneeling barbell rollouts before progressing to standing variations.
Side Plank Oblique Crunch
The Side Plank Oblique Crunch is an effective core exercise that strengthens the obliques and improves stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in a side plank position with your elbow directly under your shoulder.
2. Place your free hand behind your head.
3. Bring your top knee toward your top elbow while engaging your obliques.
4. Return to the starting position and repeat before switching sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your body in a straight line throughout the movement.
2. Avoid letting your hips drop.
3. Perform controlled movements for maximum effectiveness.
Medicine Ball Sit-Up Throw
The Medicine Ball Sit-Up Throw is a dynamic core exercise that builds explosive strength and coordination.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the floor with your knees bent and hold a medicine ball at chest level.
2. Perform a sit-up while keeping the ball close to your chest.
3. At the top of the sit-up, explosively throw the ball forward or to a partner.
4. Catch the ball and return to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Engage your core to generate power.
2. Use a controlled motion when catching and lowering the ball.
3. Choose an appropriate weight for the medicine ball to prevent strain.
Side Bent
The Side Bent exercise targets the obliques and helps improve lateral core strength and flexibility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Place one hand on your hip and extend the other arm overhead.
3. Slowly bend to the side, keeping your torso aligned.
4. Return to the starting position and repeat on the opposite side.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid leaning forward or backward.
2. Move slowly and engage your core.
3. Use a dumbbell for added resistance if needed.
Leg Scissors
The Leg Scissors exercise strengthens the lower abs and improves coordination.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie flat on your back with your hands under your lower back for support.
2. Lift your legs off the ground slightly.
3. Move your legs in a crisscross motion, alternating their positions.
4. Continue the movement for a set duration or reps.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your lower back pressed to the floor.
2. Move your legs in a controlled manner.
3. Avoid holding your breath—breathe naturally.
Abdominal Bracing
Abdominal Bracing is a foundational exercise that strengthens the core and improves stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand or lie on your back in a neutral position.
2. Tighten your abdominal muscles as if bracing for impact.
3. Maintain the contraction while breathing normally.
4. Hold the brace for a few seconds before relaxing.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid holding your breath—focus on controlled breathing.
2. Engage all core muscles, not just the upper abs.
3. Practice this technique in other exercises to enhance core stability.
Lying Toe Touches
The Lying Toe Touches exercise targets the upper abs and improves core stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with your legs extended straight up toward the ceiling.
2. Extend your arms upward, reaching toward your toes.
3. Engage your core and lift your upper body off the ground as you reach for your toes.
4. Lower back down slowly and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your legs straight and avoid swinging.
2. Use your core muscles to lift rather than pulling with your neck.
3. Perform slow and controlled movements.
Dumbbell Floor Wipers
The Dumbbell Floor Wipers exercise strengthens the core, obliques, and shoulders.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back and hold a dumbbell with both hands above your chest.
2. Lift your legs off the ground and keep them straight.
3. Lower your legs to one side without touching the floor.
4. Bring your legs back up and lower them to the opposite side.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your arms extended and stable.
2. Control the movement to engage your core effectively.
3. Avoid letting your lower back arch excessively.
Side Bridge Hip Abduction
The Side Bridge Hip Abduction is a great core and glute exercise that enhances lateral stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in a side plank position with your forearm on the ground.
2. Keep your body in a straight line.
3. Lift your top leg upward while maintaining balance.
4. Lower the leg back down and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Engage your core and glutes throughout the movement.
2. Keep your hips from sagging.
3. Perform slow and controlled repetitions.
Cable Half Kneeling Pallof Press
The Cable Half Kneeling Pallof Press strengthens the core and improves anti-rotational stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Attach a cable at chest height and hold the handle with both hands.
2. Get into a half-kneeling position with your side facing the machine.
3. Press the handle straight out in front of you without rotating your torso.
4. Bring the handle back to your chest and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged to resist rotation.
2. Maintain an upright posture throughout the movement.
3. Use a moderate resistance to ensure control.
Snap Jumps
Snap Jumps are a fast-paced, explosive exercise that strengthens the core and improves agility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in a high plank position with hands under your shoulders.
2. Jump both feet forward, bringing your knees toward your chest.
3. Quickly extend your legs back to the starting position.
4. Repeat the movement in a controlled yet explosive manner.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged for stability.
2. Land softly to reduce impact on the joints.
3. Maintain a steady rhythm for endurance.
Side Plank Leg Raises
The Side Plank Leg Raises exercise strengthens the core, obliques, and hip abductors.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in a side plank position with your forearm on the ground and your body in a straight line.
2. Keep your top leg straight and lift it upward as high as possible.
3. Lower your leg back down in a controlled manner.
4. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged and hips stable.
2. Avoid letting your lower back sag.
3. Perform slow and controlled movements to maximize effectiveness.
Reverse Plank Kicks
The Reverse Plank Kicks exercise targets the core, glutes, and shoulders while improving flexibility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in a reverse plank position with your hands behind you and legs extended straight.
2. Engage your core and lift one leg upward while maintaining balance.
3. Lower the leg back down and switch sides.
4. Continue alternating legs for the desired repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your hips lifted and your body in a straight line.
2. Move with control to avoid unnecessary swinging.
3. Maintain a steady breathing pattern throughout the exercise.
Hindu Push-ups
Hindu Push-ups are a dynamic bodyweight exercise that builds upper body strength and flexibility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in a downward dog position with hands and feet on the ground.
2. Lower your chest towards the floor, moving in a swooping motion.
3. Arch your back as you press your chest forward and extend your arms.
4. Return to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Engage your core and maintain smooth transitions.
2. Keep your elbows slightly bent to reduce joint strain.
3. Breathe deeply and move with control.
Bear Crawl
The Bear Crawl is a full-body exercise that enhances coordination, stability, and strength.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start on all fours with your knees slightly off the ground.
2. Move your opposite hand and foot forward simultaneously.
3. Continue crawling forward while maintaining a neutral spine.
4. Reverse the movement to crawl backward if desired.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged and your movements controlled.
2. Maintain a steady breathing rhythm.
3. Avoid lifting your hips too high.
High Knee Skips
High Knee Skips improve coordination, cardiovascular endurance, and lower body strength.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
2. Jump off one foot while driving the opposite knee up towards your chest.
3. Land softly and immediately switch to the other leg.
4. Continue alternating legs in a skipping motion.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Maintain an upright posture and engage your core.
2. Pump your arms to increase momentum.
3. Land softly to reduce impact on your joints.
Double Crunches
The Double Crunch is a core-strengthening exercise that targets both the upper and lower abdominal muscles.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Place your hands behind your head with your elbows out to the sides.
3. Simultaneously lift your upper body and bring your knees toward your chest.
4. Lower back down with control and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Engage your core throughout the movement.
2. Avoid pulling on your neck with your hands.
3. Perform slow, controlled reps for better effectiveness.
Toe Reaches
Toe Reaches target the upper abdominal muscles and improve flexibility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with your legs extended straight up towards the ceiling.
2. Reach your hands toward your toes while lifting your upper body off the ground.
3. Slowly lower back down and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged and avoid using momentum.
2. Move with control and exhale as you reach up.
3. Focus on using your abdominal muscles, not your neck.
Sit-ups
Sit-ups are a classic abdominal exercise that strengthens the core and improves endurance.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Place your hands behind your head or cross them over your chest.
3. Engage your core and lift your torso towards your knees.
4. Lower back down slowly and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid pulling on your neck to lift yourself up.
2. Perform slow and controlled movements.
3. Engage your core throughout the exercise.
Side Plank
The Side Plank is an isometric core exercise that strengthens the obliques and improves balance.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your side with your forearm on the ground and your feet stacked.
2. Lift your hips off the floor, keeping your body in a straight line.
3. Hold the position for the desired duration.
4. Switch sides and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged and your hips lifted.
2. Avoid letting your body sag.
3. Breathe steadily and maintain good posture.
Plank Leg Lift
Plank Leg Lift is a core-strengthening exercise that also engages the glutes and lower back.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in a forearm plank position with your body in a straight line.
2. Engage your core and lift one leg off the ground.
3. Hold for a second, then lower the leg back down.
4. Repeat on the other side.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your hips stable and avoid excessive movement.
2. Engage your core throughout the exercise.
3. Perform slow and controlled repetitions.
Plank Knee to Elbow
Plank Knee to Elbow is a dynamic core exercise that engages the obliques and improves balance.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in a high plank position with your hands under your shoulders.
2. Bring your right knee toward your right elbow while keeping your core engaged.
3. Return to the starting position and repeat with the left knee.
4. Continue alternating sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your body in a straight line without sagging your hips.
2. Move with control and avoid rushing the movement.
3. Engage your core throughout the exercise.
Russian Twist
Russian Twist is a rotational core exercise that strengthens the obliques and improves stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet slightly lifted.
2. Hold your hands together or a weight in front of you.
3. Rotate your torso to the right, then to the left, while keeping your core engaged.
4. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back straight and avoid rounding your shoulders.
2. Move with control and engage your obliques.
3. If needed, place your feet on the floor for stability.
Plank
The Plank is a fundamental core-strengthening exercise that improves stability and endurance.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in a forearm plank position with your elbows under your shoulders.
2. Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
3. Hold the position for the desired duration while engaging your core.
4. Avoid letting your hips sag or lifting them too high.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core tight and your glutes engaged.
2. Maintain steady breathing.
3. Start with shorter holds and gradually increase time.
Leg Pull-in Knee-ups
Leg Pull-in Knee-ups target the lower abs and improve core strength.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the edge of a bench or mat with your hands behind you for support.
2. Extend your legs out in front of you.
3. Pull your knees toward your chest, engaging your core.
4. Extend your legs back out and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your movement controlled and avoid using momentum.
2. Engage your core throughout the exercise.
3. Breathe steadily as you move.
Glute Bridge
Glute Bridge is a lower-body and core exercise that strengthens the glutes and hamstrings.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Press through your heels to lift your hips toward the ceiling.
3. Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower back down with control.
4. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged and avoid overarching your back.
2. Press evenly through both feet.
3. Perform slow and controlled movements for better muscle activation.
Hollow Hold
Hollow Hold is an isometric core exercise that builds endurance and strength in the abdominals.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with your arms extended overhead and legs straight.
2. Lift your arms, shoulders, and legs off the ground, keeping your lower back pressed into the floor.
3. Hold the position while engaging your core.
4. Maintain a steady breath and hold for the desired duration.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your lower back in contact with the floor to avoid strain.
2. Modify by bending your knees if needed.
3. Engage your core throughout the hold.
Long Arm Crunch
Long Arm Crunch is a variation of the traditional crunch that increases core engagement.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with your arms extended straight behind your head.
2. Keep your legs bent and feet flat on the floor.
3. Engage your core and lift your upper back off the ground.
4. Lower back down with control and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid pulling with your arms; use your core muscles.
2. Move with a slow and controlled motion.
3. Keep your lower back on the floor throughout the movement.
Half Wipers
Half Wipers is a rotational core exercise that targets the obliques and lower abs.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with your legs raised and knees bent at 90 degrees.
2. Lower your legs to one side while keeping your core engaged.
3. Return to the center and lower them to the opposite side.
4. Repeat the movement while maintaining control.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Move slowly to maximize core engagement.
2. Keep your shoulders on the floor.
3. Engage your core to control the movement.
Jackknife Sit-ups (V-Up)
Jackknife Sit-ups, also known as V-Ups, are an advanced core exercise that targets the entire abdominal region.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie flat on your back with your arms extended overhead and legs straight.
2. Simultaneously lift your arms and legs toward each other.
3. Contract your abs at the top, forming a V-shape.
4. Lower back down with control and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Move with control to avoid using momentum.
2. Engage your core throughout the movement.
3. Keep your lower back on the floor at the start of the movement.
Flutter Kick
Flutter Kicks are a lower abdominal exercise that also engages the hip flexors.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with your hands under your lower back for support.
2. Lift your legs off the ground and keep them straight.
3. Alternate kicking your legs up and down in a controlled manner.
4. Continue the movement for the desired duration.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your lower back pressed into the floor.
2. Move with control to engage your core.
3. Breathe steadily throughout the exercise.
Standing Side Bend
Standing Side Bend is an effective exercise for stretching and strengthening the obliques.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Place one hand on your hip and extend the other arm overhead.
3. Slowly bend your torso to the side while keeping your core engaged.
4. Return to the starting position and repeat on the other side.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid leaning forward or backward; focus on lateral movement.
2. Move slowly and with control.
3. Engage your core throughout the movement.
Suspended Ab Fall-out
Suspended Ab Fall-out is an advanced core exercise using suspension straps to engage the abs and shoulders.
To perform the exercise:
1. Hold onto suspension straps with your arms extended in front of you.
2. Lean forward while keeping your body straight.
3. Extend your arms further forward while engaging your core.
4. Pull yourself back to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core tight to prevent arching in the lower back.
2. Move slowly to maximize control.
3. Adjust strap length for different levels of difficulty.
TRX Mountain Climber
TRX Mountain Climber is a core-strengthening exercise performed with suspension straps.
To perform the exercise:
1. Place your feet in the TRX straps and get into a plank position.
2. Bring one knee towards your chest while keeping the other leg extended.
3. Quickly switch legs in a running motion.
4. Continue alternating for the desired duration.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back straight and core engaged.
2. Move with control to maintain stability.
3. Avoid bouncing or letting your hips drop.
Side Plank Knee to Elbow
Side Plank Knee to Elbow is a dynamic core exercise that targets the obliques.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in a side plank position with your body aligned.
2. Bring your top knee toward your elbow while engaging your core.
3. Extend your leg back to the starting position.
4. Repeat for the desired reps, then switch sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your hips elevated throughout the movement.
2. Engage your obliques for maximum effect.
3. Move in a slow and controlled manner.
Bodyweight Skull Crushers
Bodyweight Skull Crushers are a triceps-focused exercise that also engages the core.
To perform the exercise:
1. Get into a plank position with your hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Lower your body by bending your elbows until your forehead nears the floor.
3. Press back up to the starting position.
4. Repeat for the desired reps.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged to maintain stability.
2. Move in a controlled manner to avoid momentum.
3. Adjust hand positioning for different difficulty levels.
Half Cross Crunch
The Half Cross Crunch is a core-strengthening exercise that targets the obliques and upper abdominal muscles, improving core stability and definition.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with one leg bent and the other extended straight.
2. Place your hands behind your head or across your chest.
3. Engage your core and lift your upper body while twisting to bring your opposite elbow toward the bent knee.
4. Lower back down with control and repeat on the same side before switching.
5. Complete the desired number of repetitions on each side.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid pulling on your neck; instead, use your abdominal muscles to lift your torso.
2. Perform the movement in a slow and controlled manner to fully engage the obliques.
3. Keep your core engaged throughout the movement to maximize effectiveness.
Cable Seated Twist on Floor
The Cable Seated Twist on Floor is a rotational core exercise that strengthens the obliques and enhances overall core stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the floor with your legs slightly bent and feet anchored or flat on the ground.
2. Hold a cable handle with both hands, keeping your arms slightly bent.
3. Engage your core and rotate your torso to one side, pulling the cable across your body.
4. Slowly return to the center and repeat on the opposite side.
5. Perform the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged to maintain stability and control throughout the movement.
2. Avoid excessive twisting of the lower back; focus on controlled, smooth movements.
3. Adjust the resistance to ensure proper form and execution.
Butterfly Sit-Up
The Butterfly Sit-Up is a core-strengthening exercise that enhances abdominal endurance while improving hip flexibility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the floor with the soles of your feet together and knees open outward.
2. Lie back until your upper body touches the ground.
3. Engage your core and sit up, reaching your hands toward your feet.
4. Slowly lower back down and repeat.
5. Perform the desired number of reps.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Maintain a steady pace to avoid using momentum.
2. Engage your core throughout the movement to maximize abdominal activation.
3. Keep your feet in contact with the ground to maintain stability.
Push-Up With Rotation
The Push-Up With Rotation is a compound exercise that strengthens the chest, shoulders, and core while improving balance and coordination.
To perform the exercise:
1. Begin in a standard push-up position with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
2. Perform a push-up, lowering your chest toward the floor in a controlled motion.
3. As you push back up, rotate your body to one side, extending your arm toward the ceiling.
4. Return to the starting position and repeat on the opposite side.
5. Perform the desired number of repetitions, alternating sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Engage your core to maintain stability throughout the movement.
2. Control your movements to avoid excessive twisting or strain on the lower back.
3. Keep your breathing steady, inhaling on the way down and exhaling as you push up.
Side Plank Rotation
The Side Plank Rotation is a dynamic core exercise that enhances oblique strength, stability, and balance.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in a side plank position with your supporting forearm on the ground and the other arm extended upward.
2. Engage your core and slowly rotate your torso, bringing your top arm under your body.
3. Return to the starting position with control.
4. Repeat for the desired number of reps, then switch sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your hips lifted to maintain a straight body alignment.
2. Move slowly and with control to fully engage the obliques.
3. Avoid letting your shoulders or hips sag during the movement.
Prone Abdominal Hollowing
Prone Abdominal Hollowing is a core activation exercise that helps strengthen the deep abdominal muscles, improving stability and posture.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie face down on the floor with your arms extended alongside your body.
2. Take a deep breath in, then exhale while drawing your belly button toward your spine.
3. Hold the contraction for a few seconds, maintaining a steady breath.
4. Relax and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your body relaxed except for the core engagement.
2. Avoid lifting your hips or tensing other muscles.
3. Perform slow, controlled breaths to maximize activation.
Hell Slide
The Hell Slide is an advanced core exercise that challenges stability, endurance, and strength through sliding movements.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in a high plank position with your feet on sliders or towels.
2. Engage your core and slide both feet forward, keeping your legs straight or slightly bent.
3. Slowly return to the starting position while maintaining core tension.
4. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Maintain a strong plank position throughout the movement.
2. Avoid arching or sagging your lower back.
3. Control the movement to avoid using momentum.
Half Frog Pose
The Half Frog Pose is a yoga-based stretch that targets the hip flexors, quadriceps, and lower back.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie face down on the floor with your legs extended.
2. Bend one knee and grab your ankle with your hand on the same side.
3. Gently pull your heel toward your glute while keeping your hips grounded.
4. Hold the stretch for 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your pelvis flat against the ground to avoid strain.
2. Breathe deeply to relax into the stretch.
3. Avoid forcing the stretch; move within a comfortable range.
Medicine Ball Crunch
The Medicine Ball Crunch is an effective core exercise that adds resistance to standard crunches, increasing abdominal strength.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a medicine ball with both hands, keeping it close to your chest.
3. Engage your core and lift your upper body toward your knees.
4. Slowly lower back down and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid using momentum; focus on controlled movements.
2. Keep your lower back in contact with the ground.
3. Exhale as you lift and inhale as you lower down.
Kettlebell Figure 8
The Kettlebell Figure 8 is a dynamic core exercise that enhances coordination, grip strength, and core stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a kettlebell in one hand.
2. Slightly bend your knees and hinge at the hips.
3. Pass the kettlebell between your legs in a figure-eight motion.
4. Keep your core engaged and maintain a steady rhythm.
5. Continue for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back straight and avoid rounding your spine.
2. Control the movement rather than relying on momentum.
3. Maintain a strong grip on the kettlebell throughout the exercise.
Ball Russian Twist Throw with Partner
The Ball Russian Twist Throw with Partner is a core-strengthening exercise that enhances rotational power and coordination.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet slightly off the ground.
2. Hold a medicine ball with both hands and lean back slightly to engage your core.
3. Rotate your torso and throw the ball to your partner.
4. Your partner catches the ball, rotates, and throws it back to you.
5. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged throughout the movement.
2. Avoid using your arms to throw; generate power from your torso.
3. Maintain a steady pace and controlled movements.
Seated Ab Crunch Machine
The Seated Ab Crunch Machine isolates the abdominal muscles by providing resistance for a more effective workout.
To perform the exercise:
1. Adjust the seat and select an appropriate weight on the machine.
2. Sit with your back against the pad and grip the handles.
3. Contract your abs to bring your upper body forward.
4. Slowly return to the starting position.
5. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid using momentum; focus on controlled movements.
2. Engage your core throughout the exercise.
3. Exhale as you crunch forward and inhale as you return.
Dumbbell Windmill
The Dumbbell Windmill is a dynamic core exercise that improves flexibility, stability, and strength.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart.
2. Hold a dumbbell in one hand overhead and extend your other arm downward.
3. Keeping your legs straight, hinge at the hips and lower your torso sideways.
4. Reach toward your foot with the free hand while keeping the dumbbell steady overhead.
5. Return to the starting position and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your eyes on the dumbbell to maintain balance.
2. Engage your core and avoid excessive twisting.
3. Perform the movement slowly and with control.
Side Lying Feet Raise
The Side Lying Feet Raise targets the obliques and hip muscles for improved core and lower body stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your side with your legs stacked.
2. Place your arm under your head for support.
3. Engage your core and lift both legs together.
4. Slowly lower them back down without touching the ground.
5. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your legs straight and together throughout the movement.
2. Engage your obliques for better stability.
3. Perform slow, controlled lifts to avoid using momentum.
Dhanurasana | Rocking Bow Pose
The Dhanurasana, or Rocking Bow Pose, is a yoga pose that stretches the back, strengthens the core, and improves flexibility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie face down on the floor with your arms at your sides.
2. Bend your knees and reach back to grasp your ankles.
3. Inhale and lift your chest and thighs off the ground.
4. Hold the position and gently rock forward and backward.
5. Release and return to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your neck relaxed and avoid straining.
2. Engage your core and back muscles for stability.
3. Breathe deeply to enhance flexibility and control.
Seated Twist With Resistance Band
The Seated Twist With Resistance Band is a core-strengthening exercise that enhances rotational stability and oblique muscle engagement.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the floor with your legs extended and wrap the resistance band around a stable object.
2. Hold the ends of the band with both hands and sit upright.
3. Rotate your torso to one side while keeping your core engaged.
4. Return to the center and twist to the opposite side.
5. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back straight and shoulders relaxed.
2. Control the movement to maximize muscle engagement.
3. Avoid using your arms to pull; let your core drive the motion.
Twist With Resistance Band
The Twist With Resistance Band is a standing rotational exercise that improves core strength and mobility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Attach the resistance band to a secure object at waist height.
2. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding the band with both hands.
3. Rotate your torso away from the anchor point while keeping your arms extended.
4. Slowly return to the starting position.
5. Repeat for the desired reps and switch sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged throughout the movement.
2. Move with control to prevent excessive momentum.
3. Breathe out as you twist and inhale as you return.
Twist Down Up With Resistance Band
The Twist Down Up With Resistance Band is a dynamic exercise that strengthens the core and enhances rotational flexibility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Secure a resistance band at a low anchor point.
2. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, gripping the band with both hands.
3. Rotate downward toward the anchor point while bending your knees slightly.
4. Explosively twist upward to the opposite side.
5. Repeat for the desired reps and switch sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core tight to stabilize the movement.
2. Avoid pulling with your arms; engage your obliques.
3. Perform the motion in a controlled manner to prevent strain.
Standing Side Bend | Gymstick
The Standing Side Bend with Gymstick is an effective exercise for targeting the oblique muscles and improving lateral flexibility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding the Gymstick behind your shoulders.
2. Keep your core engaged and spine neutral.
3. Bend your torso to one side while keeping your lower body stable.
4. Return to the center and repeat on the opposite side.
5. Continue alternating for the desired reps.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid bending forward or backward.
2. Keep the movement slow and controlled.
3. Engage your obliques for maximum effect.
Banded Lying Leg And Hip Raise
The Banded Lying Leg And Hip Raise strengthens the lower abs and hip flexors by adding resistance to a traditional leg raise.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with a resistance band secured around your feet.
2. Place your hands by your sides for stability.
3. Lift your legs toward the ceiling while keeping them straight.
4. At the top, engage your core to lift your hips off the ground.
5. Slowly lower back to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid arching your lower back.
2. Use a slow, controlled motion.
3. Keep your core engaged throughout the movement.
Banded Jack Knife Sit-Up
The Banded Jack Knife Sit-Up is an advanced core exercise that enhances abdominal strength and stability by incorporating resistance bands.
To perform the exercise:
1. Attach a resistance band to a stable anchor and loop it around your feet.
2. Lie on your back with legs extended and arms reaching overhead.
3. Simultaneously lift your legs and upper body, reaching towards your feet.
4. Squeeze your core at the top and slowly lower back to the starting position.
5. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Engage your core to avoid using momentum.
2. Keep movements slow and controlled.
3. Exhale as you lift and inhale as you lower.
Down to Up Twist | Gymstick
The Down to Up Twist with Gymstick strengthens the obliques and improves rotational mobility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding the Gymstick with both hands.
2. Rotate your torso downward towards one side.
3. Engage your core and twist back up to the opposite side.
4. Repeat the movement for the desired reps, then switch sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your movements controlled and deliberate.
2. Avoid using your arms to pull; let your core drive the motion.
3. Breathe out as you twist upwards.
Bicycle Crunch | Gymstick
The Bicycle Crunch with Gymstick is a variation of the classic bicycle crunch that enhances core engagement using a Gymstick.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with the Gymstick behind your shoulders.
2. Lift your legs and bend your knees at a 90-degree angle.
3. Rotate your torso while bringing one elbow towards the opposite knee.
4. Extend the other leg straight, then switch sides in a pedaling motion.
5. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid pulling on your neck; engage your core instead.
2. Keep movements slow and controlled.
3. Maintain a steady breathing rhythm.
Plank Jacks / Extended Leg
Plank Jacks with Extended Leg is a dynamic core exercise that improves stability, endurance, and overall strength.
To perform the exercise:
1. Get into a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders.
2. Keep your core tight and jump both feet outward like a jumping jack.
3. Quickly return your feet to the starting position.
4. Repeat at a controlled pace for the desired duration.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your hips level and avoid sagging.
2. Engage your abs throughout the movement.
3. Maintain a steady breathing rhythm.
